subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Should agent-owned Gateway cron cleanup become part of the canonical `agents delete` contract now, or may experimental Claw removal remain the sole owner while ordinary agent deletion can leave those jobs behind?
rationale: The assigned review explicitly identifies a cross-feature ownership invariant, while the branch intentionally preserves ordinary deletion behavior; code review cannot choose the permanent public lifecycle contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Make canonical deletion own cron teardown
options.body: Require `agents delete` to durably remove agent-owned cron jobs and let Claw removal layer only provenance-specific cleanup around that shared operation.

options.title: Accept the experimental split temporarily
options.body: Allow Claw removal to own cron teardown for this feature, document the ordinary-delete limitation, and track a bounded core follow-up before expanding the surface.

options.title: Pause the Claw stack
options.body: Defer this slice until the broader Claw lifecycle and deletion ownership direction is approved as a coherent product plan.

recommendation.title: Make canonical deletion own cron teardown
recommendation.body: Require `agents delete` to durably remove agent-owned cron jobs and let Claw removal layer only provenance-specific cleanup around that shared operation.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned to the PR and raised the concrete canonical-deletion contract concern.
